sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared types
sections.what: Brings in the shared request helper and the scan data types, re-exports those types for other screens, and sets the Reality Scan base route.
sections.why: Likely reason: other screens can import every scan type from this one file.
sections.watch_out: The long relative import path must match the folder layout, or every screen that uses these types will fail to load.

sections.name: DeckApi, SCAN_DECK_API, DeckApiContext, useDeckApi, AssistantAction
sections.title: Settings for shared slide screens
sections.what: Defines the route settings that let a second tool, Lessons Learnt, reuse the same slide screens with its own routes. It also lists the assistant actions: chat, edit, research and reverify.
sections.why: The comment says Lessons Learnt mounts the same routes under its own base, so the screens are shared.
sections.watch_out: A new assistant action must be added to this list and also handled by the server.

sections.name: ScanScope
sections.title: Scope shape for a new run
sections.what: Describes the simpler scope sent when creating a run: industries, segments and projects.
sections.why: Likely reason: it matches what the server accepts at run creation.
sections.watch_out: The scope in the index file has more fields, so the two shapes can drift apart.

sections.name: errorStatus
sections.title: Reading the error status
sections.what: Pulls the three-digit HTTP status code, such as 409, back out of an error message.
sections.why: The shared request helper puts the status at the start of each error message, and screens need it to react differently to each error.
sections.watch_out: This works only while error messages start with three digits and a colon.

sections.name: errorText, deckKey
sections.title: Readable error text and deck cache key
sections.what: Turns an error into a short readable message, unwrapping a JSON body if one is present. Also builds the cache key used to store and refresh a run's deck.
sections.why: Users should see clear messages, and the cache key must be the same everywhere so the deck refreshes after a save.
sections.watch_out: If the cache key format changes, a saved deck may no longer refresh on screen.

sections.name: createScanRun
sections.title: Create a scan run
sections.what: Sends a scope to the server to create a run, and returns the new run's ID.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The index page creates runs with its own request, so this helper may be unused in the visible files.
sections.watch_out: Check whether any caller uses it before changing its behaviour.

sections.name: fetchDeck
sections.title: Load a deck
sections.what: Gets the saved slide deck for a run from the server.
sections.why: Likely reason: the analysis view needs the deck to draw the chart.
sections.watch_out: The server may reply with conflict or not found, and callers must handle those cases.

sections.name: patchDeckText
sections.title: Save one text edit
sections.what: Saves the new text of one element on one slide, along with the revision the editor started from. It returns the updated deck.
sections.why: Likely reason: sending the revision lets the server refuse edits made on an outdated copy.
sections.watch_out: An outdated revision is rejected, so the screen must reload before retrying.

sections.name: askAssistant
sections.title: Ask the assistant
sections.what: Sends a message to the deck assistant about a slide or element, with the action type and revision, and returns the updated deck.
sections.why: Reason for sending the revision not stated beyond matching the other saves.
sections.watch_out: The reply is a whole deck, so the caller must replace its local copy rather than merge it.

sections.name: decideProposal
sections.title: Apply or dismiss a suggestion
sections.what: Sends the user's decision on one assistant suggestion, to apply it or dismiss it, along with the revision. It returns the updated deck.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user makes the final call on each suggested change.
sections.watch_out: The revision must be current, or the server will refuse the decision.

sections.name: downloadDeckPptx, assetUrl
sections.title: Download PowerPoint and image paths
sections.what: Gets the deck as a PowerPoint file and saves it in the browser, using the file name the server gives when available. It also builds the web address for template images.
sections.why: Likely reason: the file must download under a sensible name, and the template images are served from a public folder.
sections.watch_out: The image address depends on the build's base path, so it breaks if that path changes.

summary: A set of helper functions that call the Reality Scan server routes for runs, slide decks, text edits, the assistant, and PowerPoint export.
purpose: Keeps all server calls for the scan's data in one file, so screens do not repeat addresses and error handling.
why: Likely reason: one shared place for addresses and error formats makes the screens simpler and more consistent.
how: It re-exports the shared data types and sets the base route. Then it defines one function for each server action: create a run, load a deck, save a text edit, ask the assistant, apply or dismiss a proposal, and download the PowerPoint file. Two helpers read the status code and a readable message back out of an error.
inputs: Run IDs, slide and element IDs, the revision number the editor last saw, text edits, assistant messages, proposal decisions, and an optional base route for other tools.
outputs: Parsed deck or run data from the server, a browser file download for the PowerPoint, and status codes and messages from errors.
risks: The revision number protects against overwriting newer changes, so an old revision will be refused by the server. Error status is read from the start of the error text, so changing how the shared request helper formats errors would break status detection. The download link is removed after one second.
debug: If a save fails, check the status code: 409 means the deck changed elsewhere, and 404 means the run or deck is missing. Check the base route if a call goes to the wrong place. For a failed download, check the response headers for the file name.
